Surah 83 is Medinan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–6} {Woe} is a word of punishment and retribution, {to those who give short measure}. Allah explained the "mutaffifin" (those who give short measure) as {those who, when they take measure from people, take in full}; that is, they take from people what is owed to them, exacting it in full without any deficiency. {But when they measure or weigh for them}; that is, when they give people their right that is due from them by measure or weight, {they cause loss}; that is, they diminish it for them, either by using short measures and scales, or by not filling the measure and the scale, or by other means. This is theft of people's wealth and a failure to be fair to them. If this is a warning against those who cheat people with measure and weight, then one who takes their wealth by force and theft is even more deserving of this warning than those who give short measure.

This noble verse shows that just as a person takes from people what is his due, he must give them everything that is theirs of wealth and transactions. Indeed, this principle extends to arguments and statements. Just as it is customary for each of two debaters to be keen to secure his own arguments, it is equally obligatory for him to clarify the argument of his opponent that the opponent does not know, and to examine his opponent's evidence just as he examines his own. In this matter, a person's fairness is recognized from his partisanship and bias, his humility from his arrogance, and his intellect from his foolishness. We ask Allah for success in every good.

Then Allah, exalted is He, warned the short-measurers and marveled at their condition and their persistence in what they were doing, saying: {Do they not think that they will be resurrected on a tremendous Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds?} The thing that emboldened them to give short measure was their lack of faith in the Last Day. Otherwise, had they believed in it and known that they would stand before Allah, who would hold them accountable for the small and the great, they would have desisted from this and repented of it.

{7–9} God Most High says: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin.﴾ This includes every wicked person among the various kinds of disbelievers, hypocrites and sinners, ﴿in Sijjin.﴾ Then He explained that by saying: ﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is? It is a written record,﴾ meaning: a book in which their evil deeds are recorded. Sijjin is a narrow, cramped place, and Sijjin is the opposite of 'Illiyyun (the high place), which is where the record of the righteous is kept, as will come. It has been said that Sijjin is the lowest part of the seventh earth, the abode and resting place of the wicked in their return.

{10–13} ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers,﴾ Then He described them by saying: ﴿who deny the Day of Recompense,﴾ meaning the Day of Requital, the day on which God judges people for their deeds. ﴿And none deny it except every transgressor﴾ against the sacred prohibitions of God, one who oversteps from the lawful into the unlawful, ﴿sinful.﴾ meaning one who commits much sin. His transgression drives him to denial, and his arrogance necessitates rejecting the truth. For this reason, ﴿when Our verses are recited to him,﴾ the signs of God that indicate the truth and the veracity of what the messengers brought, he denies them, opposes them, and says: these are ﴿tales of the ancients,﴾ meaning the fabrications of earlier generations and the stories of past nations, not from God, out of arrogance and obstinacy.

{14–17} As for the one who is fair and whose aim is the clear truth, he does not deny the Day of Judgement, because God has established for him decisive proofs and clear evidences that make it the certainty of truth, and it stands to their insight as the sun stands to the eyes. This is unlike the one whose earnings have rusted over his heart and whose sins have covered it; he is veiled from the truth. For this reason he is recompensed by being veiled from God just as his heart was veiled [in this world] from the signs of God. ﴿Then indeed they﴾ — despite this severe punishment — ﴿will surely burn in Hellfire.﴾ ﴿Then it will be said﴾ to them, as rebuke and reproach: ﴿This is what you used to deny.﴾ So He mentioned three kinds of punishment for them: the punishment of Hellfire, the punishment of reproach and blame, and the punishment of being veiled from the Lord of the worlds, which entails His displeasure and wrath against them, and which is greater for them than the punishment of the Fire.

The implication of the verse indicates that the believers will see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection and in Paradise, and will take pleasure in looking at Him more than in any other delight, will rejoice in His address, and will be delighted by His nearness, as God mentioned in several verses of the Qur'an, and the transmission of this from the Messenger of God ﷺ is widely attested.

In these verses there is a warning against sins, for they accumulate upon the heart and cover it little by little until its light is extinguished and its insight dies, so that realities are inverted for it, and it sees falsehood as truth and truth as falsehood. This is among the greatest punishments of sins.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 83, verses 18–28:

{18–21} When He mentioned that the record of the wicked (fujjar) is in the lowest and narrowest of places, He mentioned that the record of the righteous (abrar) is in the highest, widest and most spacious of places, and that their inscribed record {is witnessed by those brought near (al-muqarrabun)}: from among the noble angels, the spirits of the prophets, the truthful ones (siddiqin) and the martyrs (shuhada'), and Allah makes mention of them in the Highest Assembly. ʿIlliyyun (ʿIlliyyun): the name for the highest part of Paradise.

{22–28} When He mentioned their record, He mentioned that they are in bliss (na'im), a term that comprises the bliss of the heart, the spirit and the body. {On couches (al-araʾik)}; i.e., on thrones adorned with beautiful furnishings, {gazing (yanzuruna)}: upon what Allah has prepared for them of bliss, and gazing upon the face of their Noble Lord. {You (the beholder) would recognise (taʿrifu)} {in their faces the radiance (nadrat) of bliss}; i.e., its splendour, freshness and brilliance; for the continuous succession of delights, joys and pleasures bestows upon the face light, beauty and radiance. {They will be given to drink (yusqawna) of a sealed (makhtum) nectar (rahiq)}: which is among the finest and most delicious of drinks. {Its seal is musk (miskun)}: It may be that the meaning is that it is sealed against anything entering it that would diminish its delight or spoil its taste, and that the seal with which it is sealed is musk. It may also be that the meaning is that what remains at the bottom of the vessel from which they drink the nectar is dregs (hathala), namely the strong musk (al-misk al-adhfar); so this sediment, which in this world is customarily poured out, will in Paradise be of this kind. {For this}: the lasting bliss whose goodness and extent none knows but Allah, {let those who strive (al-mutanafisun) strive (fal-yatanafasi)}; i.e., let them race to hasten toward it and toward the deeds that lead to it; for this is the worthiest thing for which precious breaths should be expended, and the most fitting thing for which the mighty men should crowd to attain. The mixture (mizaj) of this drink is {from Tasnim}: which is a spring {from which those brought near drink}: pure (safan), and it is the highest of the drinks of Paradise absolutely; therefore it is exclusively for those brought near, who are the highest of creation in rank, and mixed for the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin); i.e., blended with the nectar and other delicious drinks.

When He, exalted is He, mentioned the recompense of the criminals and the recompense of the good-doers, and the great difference between them, He informed that the criminals used to mock the believers in this world and ridicule them. ﴿They laughed﴾ at them, and ﴿winked﴾ at them as they passed by, out of contempt and disdain for them. Despite this, you see them secure, with fear never occurring to their minds. ﴿When they returned to their people﴾, whether in the morning or the evening, ﴿they returned jesting﴾, meaning joyful and delighted. This is the utmost of deception: they combined the greatest wrongdoing with security in this world, as if a book and a covenant from God had come to them that they are among the people of happiness. They also judged for themselves that they are the people of guidance and that the believers are astray, fabricating against God and daring to speak about Him without knowledge. He, exalted, said: ﴿But they were not sent as guardians over them﴾, meaning they were not sent as agents over the believers, charged with preserving their deeds, so that they would be eager to label them as misguided. This from them is nothing but obstinacy, opposition, and trifling, which has no basis and no proof.

For this reason their recompense in the Hereafter is of the same kind as their deeds. He, exalted, said: ﴿So today﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾, when they see them in the surging of the torment, turning over, while what they used to invent has vanished from them. The believers will be in the utmost comfort and tranquility ﴿upon couches﴾, which are adorned thrones, ﴿gazing﴾ at the bounty that God has prepared for them, and gazing at the Face of their Generous Lord. ﴿Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?﴾, meaning: have they been recompensed in kind for their deeds? Just as they laughed at the believers in this world and accused them of misguidance, the believers laugh at them in the Hereafter, when they see them in the punishment and the torment, which is the requital of error and misguidance. Yes, they have been repaid for what they used to do, as a matter of justice and wisdom from God. And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

When He, exalted is He, mentioned the recompense of the criminals and the recompense of the good-doers, and the great difference between them, He informed that the criminals used to mock the believers in this world and ridicule them. ﴿They laughed﴾ at them, and ﴿winked﴾ at them as they passed by, out of contempt and disdain for them. Despite this, you see them secure, with fear never occurring to their minds. ﴿When they returned to their people﴾, whether in the morning or the evening, ﴿they returned jesting﴾, meaning joyful and delighted. This is the utmost of deception: they combined the greatest wrongdoing with security in this world, as if a book and a covenant from God had come to them that they are among the people of happiness. They also judged for themselves that they are the people of guidance and that the believers are astray, fabricating against God and daring to speak about Him without knowledge. He, exalted, said: ﴿But they were not sent as guardians over them﴾, meaning they were not sent as agents over the believers, charged with preserving their deeds, so that they would be eager to label them as misguided. This from them is nothing but obstinacy, opposition, and trifling, which has no basis and no proof.

For this reason their recompense in the Hereafter is of the same kind as their deeds. He, exalted, said: ﴿So today﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾, when they see them in the surging of the torment, turning over, while what they used to invent has vanished from them. The believers will be in the utmost comfort and tranquility ﴿upon couches﴾, which are adorned thrones, ﴿gazing﴾ at the bounty that God has prepared for them, and gazing at the Face of their Generous Lord. ﴿Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?﴾, meaning: have they been recompensed in kind for their deeds? Just as they laughed at the believers in this world and accused them of misguidance, the believers laugh at them in the Hereafter, when they see them in the punishment and the torment, which is the requital of error and misguidance. Yes, they have been repaid for what they used to do, as a matter of justice and wisdom from God. And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
